sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama) — unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax differentiation
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: civil-law tradition (Commercial Code) with strong Anglo-American influence in corporate law, private-interest foundations (Ley 25 of 1995), trusts, and the international shipping registry
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1991)
Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Panama–Republic of Korea Income Tax Convention (signed 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Panama General Corporation Law (Ley 32 of 1927, as amended); AML/CFT framework under Ley 23 of 27 April 2015, as amended by Ley 70 of 2019; Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF) regulated by Executive Decree 126 of 2020; Ley 129 of 2020 on tax transparency; Ley 392 of 2024 reinstating the UBO register after the 2023 Supreme Court ruling; Public Registry regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of each UBO's passport identification page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the country-of-origin competent authority; Consular Legalization if the origin state is not a Hague Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or equivalent corporate existence proof when a UBO is a corporate entity
Power of attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent and founding attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified Spanish translation required for registry use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential or business address of each UBO and director (bank statement or public utility invoice dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or utility provider in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/KYC banker's reference letter for each beneficial owner (recommended for Stripe Billing and Direct Debit payment-rail onboarding)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letterhead with notarized signature and Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UAF (Panama) domestic financial-crime list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and FATF public statements; PEP identification via written AML questionnaire; enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs per Ley 23/2015 (as amended); any positive hit is escalated to the AML compliance officer and may constitute grounds for refusal to proceed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Mercantil (e-Registro / consulta de nombres; www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registry language is Spanish; names must be expressible in Latin (Roman) script and phonetically distinctive in Spanish; identical or confusingly similar names already inscribed are rejected on a first-to-file basis; foreign-language names are admissible only when converted to Roman-script spelling.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registry refuses a name for identical or phonetic similarity, the filing attorney must obtain the written refusal and file a formal administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) with the Dirección General del Registro Público within 5 working days or the shorter period stated in the refusal notice; a refused name cannot be re-filed until the appeal is resolved or a modification is admitted. The certificate of search remains valid for 30 calendar days and is generally not renewable, so incorporation must be presented within that window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. A low-risk vertical industrial ERP/CRM SaaS entity without regulated activities may maintain its registered office at the licensed resident agent's address; no local physical staff or premises are required where the Sociedad Anónima is tax non-resident and conducts offshore activities only.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this segment (estimated 5–10% annual probability). No physical stock, no regulated Panamanian activity, and no local treasury function materially reduce unannounced on-site inspection risk, provided the UBO register filing and resident-agent records are kept current.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance certificate (certificado de búsqueda y no inscripción)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Sección de Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff; approx. USD 20 per certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial protocolization of articles of incorporation (pacto social and bylaws)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff by number of folios; market range USD 80–150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and filing of the incorporation dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark USD 600–1,200 for a standard low-risk S.A.
Statutory inscription tariff scaled to authorized capital; approx. USD 250 at standard capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed resident agent (agente residente) — first year
Registered office address service — first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; commonly bundled within the agent fee where a single address is used

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register (RUBF) statutory initial filing — DGI fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee schedule under Executive Decree 126/2020

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register preparation and electronic filing support
Pre-incorporation AML/KYC file: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and FATF screening of UBOs and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk vertical SaaS/CRM structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal, share certificate book, and statutory minute/share books with registry stamping
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public Registry (book stamping) and commercial stationer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-folio stamping tariff plus market supplies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization and certified Spanish translation of UBO documents (approx. 5 instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería) and competent authorities of origin states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document apostille fee (approx. USD 10–30) plus certified translation at market rates

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: General Corporation Law of Panama (Ley 32 de 1927, as amended by Ley 5 de 2013), Articles 1–40 on incorporation, corporate capital, registered office, directors and officers; supplementary provisions of the Código de Comercio of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Mercantile Registry Division, Registro Público de Panamá, Panama City, Republic of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución) registered with the Registro Público de Panamá, resulting in the certified Certificate of Incorporation for the Sociedad Anónima.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Sociedad Anónima; the authorized capital is divided into shares with a nominal par value or no par value, and no escrow account or initial paid-in capital deposit is required by Panama law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the subscriptions to the corporation’s authorized common shares are hereby ratified and fully subscribed as set out in the Share Subscription Registry, with no escrow deposit required; RESOLVED: that the registered office located in the Republic of Panama, as designated in the Public Deed of Incorporation, is adopted as the corporation’s statutory domicile, and the appointed Resident Agent is confirmed; RESOLVED: that [President], [Secretary], and [Treasurer] are appointed as initial officers, each to serve until the next shareholders’ meeting; and RESOLVED: that the officers are authorized to execute all filings and open bank accounts required for commencement of operations, such measures to take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Name Verification Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name-clearance request to the Registro Público, proposing at least two alternative corporate names for the Sociedad Anónima. Pay the applicable search fee and obtain the Negative Certificate (Certificado de Negativa) confirming that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or identity documents of the subscribers
First, second and third preferred corporate names
Brief statement of corporate purpose (vertical ERP and CRM software services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, file for a new name clearance using the alternate name list; no formal appeal is required because the applicant may simply resubmit alternative names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct Panamanian counsel to prepare the Escritura Pública incorporating the Sociedad Anónima. The deed must state the corporate name, statutory purpose, term, authorized capital, registered office, Resident Agent, directors and officers. All subscribers or their legal representatives must personally appear or be represented before the notary to execute the deed in Spanish.
required_dossiers: Corporate name clearance certificate obtained in Step 1
Identification documents of all subscribers or attorneys-in-fact
Draft of the Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws)
Written consent of the appointed Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises any irregularity in the draft deed, the notary will return the draft for correction without prejudice. Counsel revises the deed, obtains new signatures where necessary, and re-requests notarial execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Public Deed in the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Registry Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarial execution, deliver the original public deed and its certified copies to the Mercantile Registry. Pay the prescribed inscription fee and provide all supporting documents. The Registry examines the deed for compliance with Law 32 of 1927 and records the corporation in the Mercantile Register.
required_dossiers: Original copy of the notarized Public Deed of Incorporation
Official payment receipt for the registry inscription fee
Name clearance certificate
Resident Agent acceptance letter and registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an 'observación' or requests corrections, file a supplemental public deed or rectification document resolving the specific objection, then resubmit the corrected document to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Inscribed Certified Copy and Company Existence Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Certification Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the 'Primera Copia Inscrita' of the public deed and a Certificate of Existence (Certificado de Existencia) attesting to the incorporation and corporate good standing. These documents serve as the official identity proof of the corporation for banks, tax authorities, and commercial counterparties.
required_dossiers: Registry folio and inscription number assigned to the corporation
Filing request form
Registry fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certified copy or certificate contains typographical or data-entry errors, the applicant files a written request for correction or erratum with the Registry, attaching the corporate identification data and any supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration and Issuance of RUC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated Sociedad Anónima for tax purposes at the DGI taxpayer-service window. Obtain the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) / RUC, register the corporation’s territorial tax obligations, and confirm the fiscal address. Where applicable, register for monthly IVA and income-tax compliance obligations.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Public Deed of Incorporation
Certificate of Existence issued by the Registro Público
Copy of the legal representative’s or resident director’s identity document
Proof of registered office address in Panama
Corporate email address and local contact statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI challenges the RUC filing or requests further verification, the corporation has ten working days to provide additional documents, correct the registration form, and resubmit through the DGI online or counter channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Book Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the corporate Shareholders Register (Libro de Registro de Acciones) and the Board of Directors Minutes Book (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva) to the Registro Público for legalization. Each book must be bound, numbered, and initialized by the Registrar in accordance with the Commercial Code and Corporation Law.
required_dossiers: RUC or NIT certificate of the corporation
Inscribed copy of the Public Deed of Incorporation
List of directors and officers appointed in the First Board Resolution
Corporate books to be legalized
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the books fail the formal legalization review, counsel corrects the binding or pagination, or submits replacement books, and a new legalization application is filed without affecting the corporate existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operation Aviso and Occupation Permit Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas / Ventanilla de Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Aviso de Operación to the Panama Municipality for a professional software and IT-services office. Declare the business activity under the ISIC 6201 category and confirm that the premises will be used solely for administrative and software development operations. Pay the municipal fee and obtain the municipal operating permit.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate issued by the DGI
Certified copies of the Public Deed of Incorporation
Proof of lease or title to the registered office premises
Identity documents of the legal representative
Description of business activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality classifies the activity under a different category, the corporation may submit an appeal and a written request for reclassification to the ISIC 6201 software-services category, attaching the corporate purpose from the Public Deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Classification Filing and Exemption Statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the environmental classification of the commercial software office. Because the business involves no industrial processing, manufacturing, or significant pollutant discharge, file a non-applicability statement or exemption registration if required. For any future physical installation, obtain the applicable MiAMBIENTE clearance before making structural or operational changes.
required_dossiers: Municipal operating permit issued in Step 7
Corporate purpose and premises description
RUC and registered office proof
Declaration of no industrial or harmful discharges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MiAMBIENTE requests an evaluation, the applicant may submit an environmental assessment form under Categoría I, pay the corresponding fee, and provide supplementary information proving the non-polluting nature of office software activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales; Ministerial oversight by Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias for commercial service licenses
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso de Operación Comercial / Aviso de Operación

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Registration/Non-mandatory: pure software and cloud-service office is not an industrial activity requiring a full EIA report; an exemption statement or low-impact registration suffices.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions; comply with municipal wastewater connection standards, general urban solid-waste disposal rules, and, if installed, backup-generator emission limits under Panamanian environmental law; all electronic waste must be documented and transferred to approved waste operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification and occupancy permit for the office premises issued by SINAPROC and the Municipality; structural load inspection if facilities are significantly modified; workplace health-and-safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) prior to employee commencement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; official taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI / e-Tax 2.0 (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa and https://etax.dgi.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident-owned Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) must: (1) complete incorporation before the Registro Público de Panamá, including appointment of a resident agent (agente residente) and filing of the public deed; (2) legalize the corporate ledger before the DGI or other competent authority as applicable; (3) file the RUC registration application (Solicitud de Inscripción / Aviso de Inscripción) with the DGI, accompanied by the notarized power of attorney, certificate of incorporation (Ficha Registral), resident agent certification, and proof of fiscal address; (4) receive the permanent RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) tax identification number; (5) register the ISIC 6201 economic activity (computer programming / vertical ERP-CRM cloud software) and any relevant sub-activities; (6) activate the DGI e-Tax account and obtain an advanced digital signature (firma avanzada) issued under Panama's authorized digital-certification framework; and (7) apply for DGI authorization to issue invoices (authorized invoice booklets or DGI-certified electronic invoicing) and for any applicable withholding registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (entity-level taxation): the S.A. is taxed as a separate corporation exclusively on Panama-source income under the territorial/source system; foreign-source income is statutorily exempt from Panamanian income tax; no pass-through or tax-transparent treatment exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid entity election is available under Panamanian law; the S.A. is mandatorily treated as a corporation. Available optional elections: (i) voluntary registration for ITBMS before breaching the B/.36,000 annual threshold, necessary to recover export-related input ITBMS credits; (ii) election of the simplified small-taxpayer regime (RISPEC) if the entity meets statutory low-revenue and low-asset thresholds; (iii) formal export zero-rating status as an exporter of services with DGI-approved documentation; (iv) no CFC or hybrid mismatch elections; economic substance and territorial-nexus documentation must be maintained to preserve the foreign-source income exemption.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panama's national VAT/general indirect tax administered by the DGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (Panamanian balboas, at par with US$) of annual gross receipts from taxable sales of goods and services; mandatory RUC and ITBMS registration once the threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold, especially for exporting SaaS/cloud entities seeking input credit recovery.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates DGI-authorized electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica de Panamá). The S.A. must generate invoices in DGI-compatible XML format through a certified billing system integrated with the vertical ERP/CRM cloud platform, transmit to the DGI via the e-Tax portal/web-services (API), obtain automated DGI fiscal authorization (validación/autorización fiscal) with digital signature and QR-code labeling, and preserve electronic books of sales and purchases; real-time clearance is phased by taxpayer category, and only DGI-validated invoices support input credits, exporter zero-rating, and refund claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are eligible for 0% ITBMS when they leave Panama to a non-resident purchaser and are covered by a valid customs export declaration. Services, including vertical cloud ERP/CRM subscriptions, qualify for 0% export treatment when rendered to a non-resident subscriber whose use/benefit occurs wholly outside Panama; the DGI examines the foreign subscriber status (foreign RUC/tax ID), absence of Panama-source exploitation, offshore platform delivery, service contract terms, and payment remitted from abroad. Pure SaaS/cloud download and access qualify if the company demonstrates the non-Panamanian nexus; related input ITBMS may be credited or refunded as an export over-credit. Panama's dollarized system imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline, but the 180-day collection window below is the customary DGI/banking evidentiary benchmark for export proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Declaración de Exportación / DUA) electronically filed where physical media, servers, or equipment leave Panama; not required for pure cloud delivery
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or courier receipt evidencing physical export (if goods are shipped)
Original DGI-authorized 0% ITBMS export invoice addressed to the non-resident client
Executed software subscription/SOW showing the foreign subscriber, delivery method, and offshore use/benefit
Inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice (abono bancario / certificación de divisas) proving receipt of funds from abroad
ERP/CRM platform usage, login, and download logs for the subscription period evidencing remote offshore fulfillment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits export zero-rating by cross-matching invoices, customs declarations, contracts, bank proceeds, and platform delivery logs. Penalties for fraudulent or improperly documented export zero-rating include retrospective reassessment at 7% ITBMS plus statutory monthly surcharges/interest, substantial fines scaled to the tax omitted (including aggravated amounts for fraud), criminal sanctions for tax crimes under Ley 76 de 2019 (defraudación tributaria) and the Código Penal, cancellation of RUC/electronic-invoicing authorization and of exporter zero-rating status, denial or clawback of ITBMS refunds, and non-deductibility of penalties; documentation must be retained for the Código Fiscal prescription period, which is extended in cases of fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama maintains no central bank, no monetary authority and no exchange control administration. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) supervises licensed banks as the de facto financial regulator, while Banco Nacional de Panamá operates merely as the State's fiscal agent, clearing agent for checks and ACH, and lender of last resort without currency issuance powers; the balboa coin is issued by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) solely as a fractional token fully backed 1:1 by the U.S. dollar.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized, freely convertible jurisdiction: the U.S. dollar is legal tender for all transactions and the balboa exists only as an accounting unit, so there are no capital account restrictions, no exchange licensing, and no prior-approval regime for dividends, intercompany loans, or equity injections. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted and profit remittance is unimpeded; the only statutory friction for foreign shareholders is Panama's territorial income tax, under which Panamanian-source profits distributed to shareholders carry a 5% withholding dividend tax (or 10% if the corporate tax made-effective threshold is bypassed), while foreign-source profits of the S.A. are distributable free of Panamanian tax. No shareholder registry filing or currency conversion certificate is required before remittance; the practical gate is instead banking compliance under Ley 23 de 2015 plus a valid Paz y Salvo Fiscal (tax clearance) for any disbursement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for export proceeds, because Panama does not issue a national fiat currency. Software and cloud service exports (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210) earned through ERP/CRM subscriptions may be held offshore indefinitely or credited directly to any SBP-licensed bank in U.S. dollars; the only obligations are the bank's suspicious-transaction reporting and the exporter's proper service-export invoicing, which in Panama requires an issued factura for exported services and inclusion of the corresponding Swift MT103 record in the annual KYC file of the exporter.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Medium as a secondary settlement rail but Low as the primary treasury account. Panama's fintech framework (Ley 142 de 2021 and SBP implementing agreements) grants SBP authorizations to locally incorporated non-bank payment providers, but there is no direct EMI licence class; offshore EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Mercury, etc.) hold only custodial client funds through correspondent partners and cannot obtain a Panamanian-style bank account number, cannot clear through ACH Panamá, and would expose the S.A. to vendor-risk AML flags if used as the principal operating account. For card collection, Stripe Billing is not directly usable by a Panama-incorporated S.A. because Panama is outside Stripe's currently published merchant-support list; the practical blueprint is a Delaware or U.S. contracting entity collecting Stripe settlements and re-invoicing PA_CORP, with monthly intercompany SWIFT sweeps; local Direct Debit collection is instead performed through ACH Panamá and card clearing through DataClave and SBP-bank acquirers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote-only onboarding is technically permitted under the SBP's risk-based onboarding rules, but Tier-1 banks in practice require physical presence of at least one director, secretary, or law-firm principal empowered by the corporate power of attorney; a fully remote foreign director must execute an apostilled corporate resolution appointing a Panamanian resident agent or attorney, who then personally attends the bank interview and signs the account mandate. SBP examinations additionally mandate a live personal interview of the ultimate beneficial owners or their official attorney-in-fact, and may accept an enhanced video KYC interview with two notarized IDs for low-risk software-export companies, but the legal entity itself must always be represented in Panama by an accredited law firm with an escritura poder and a current certificate of good standing from the Registro Público.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ghost-company profile: the S.A. has no Panamanian payroll, no physical premises, and a single offshore director, generating the classic shell risk for banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a signed office sublease for a Panama City business centre, a resident-agent engagement letter, the Aviso de Operación filed with MICI, payroll records for at least one Panamanian employee or contracted compliance officer, and a substance narrative linking the ERP/CRM software operations to the Panamanian domicile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: the S.A. is held through layered entities or a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with no clear individual UBO chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File and present the certificated declaration of final beneficiary issued by the Registro Público's Beneficiario Final unit, a notarized corporate-organ chart tracing from the S.A. founder shares to each individual UBO, the foundation deed, and a local-counsel AML opinion identifying all natural persons with at least 10% interest; for every interposed company attach its own UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital mismatch: registered capital of USD 10,000 versus declared subscription revenue of several million USD, suggesting unverified treasury inflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the notarized capital increase resolution, a Swift MT103 trail of the actual capital injection, a 12-month pro-forma cash flow backed by signed cloud-subscription contracts, audit-reviewed financial statements from a Panamanian CPA, and bank statements evidencing that card and direct-debit traffic behaves as operating revenue rather than equity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or politically exposed client exposure in ERP/CRM contracts with LATAM government-owned enterprises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the completed KYB and sanctions-screening pack of each contracting counterparty covering OFAC, EU, UN, and UK consolidated lists, a legal opinion categorizing the transaction as licensed software and cloud services, executed data-processing agreements, evidence of no cash or digital-asset settlement, and an annual independent AML audit engagement letter.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Unica) and Pagare voucher payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Caja de Ahorros (bank collector) on behalf of the Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas (MEF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Staggered by the last digit of the corporate RUC: RUC ending 0-1 due by 31 January; 2-3 due by 28/29 February; 4-5 due by 31 March; 6-7 due by 30 April; 8-9 due by 31 May of the applicable annual cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax plus moratory interest of 1% per month; failure to pay for two consecutive fiscal years may cause the Registro Publico de Panama to administratively cancel the corporate registration as extincta, requiring reinstatement fees and payment of arrears

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaracion Jurada Anual de Renta, Form 140) including nil or territorial-source income position
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas (MEF), submitted through the SIME-DGI electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March of the year following the fiscal year end (default fiscal year is calendar year, ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects the S.A. to a 10% surcharge on any assessed tax, monthly moratory interest of 1%, and administrative fines under the Codigo Fiscal; persistent non-filing bars issuance of tax clearance certificates and allows DGI presumptive assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual No-Economic-Activity Sworn Statement or active-operation update submitted concurrently with the annual income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas (MEF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March of the year following the fiscal year end, aligned with the Form 140 filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete declaration is treated as non-filing of the annual return, triggering the same 10% surcharge and monthly interest regime plus administrative fines up to USD 5,000 under Codigo Fiscal sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) data confirmation and update filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Nacional de Beneficiarios Finales, administrated by the Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas (MEF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the calendar-year window published by the Registry; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be updated within 30 days of the event, superseding the annual cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation or late update attracts fines of up to USD 500 per declaration, suspension of validation certificates, and administrative enforcement under Ley 129 de 2021; wilful omission may additionally block DGI and Registro Publico procedures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Panamanian licensed public accountant where annual gross revenues exceed USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000; audit also compulsory for banks, insurers, fiduciaries, and public-interest entities; low-revenue S.A.s may present unaudited financial statements unless shareholders or statutory lenders require an audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama; SMEs may apply IFRS for SMEs; financial statements are expressed in Balboas/US Dollars under a territorial tax accounting base

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every S.A. registered in the Registro Nacional de Beneficiarios Finales must access the official online portal and annually reconfirm the identity, nationality, tax residence, and precise shareholding percentage of each ultimate beneficial owner; nil-change companies must still complete the annual confirmation to preserve the validation certificate; any share transfer or ownership restructuring requires a fresh update within 30 days of the transaction, irrespective of the annual cycle
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors and Officers (Libro de Registro de Directores y Funcionarios)
Minute Book of Shareholders Assemblies (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)
Minute Book of Board of Directors (Libro de Actas de Directorio)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350-USD 1,500 per year for resident legal agent, registered office, and basic compliance administration services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000-USD 6,500 for a certified independent audit of an inactive or low-activity cloud software S.A.; audit not mandatory below the statutory revenue and asset thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on Panamanian-source income for a standard Sociedad Anónima (S.A.); additional complementary dividend withholding applies at distribution.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama operates a strict territorial tax system; foreign-source income is outside the charge to corporate income tax. No general patent box or software tax holiday. Specific incentives include: (i) Panama Pacifico regime — 100% income tax exemption for up to 25 years, subject to relocation and import substitution conditions; (ii) SEM (Multinational Company Headquarters) tax regime under Law 41 of 2007 — preferential income tax rates of 5% or 15% on qualifying services, exemption from remittance tax, and accelerated depreciation. Neither incentive applies automatically to a low-risk vertical CRM cloud entity; the said entity must apply under the corresponding sectoral rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 2 “Declaración Jurada de Renta de Personas Jurídicas” filed through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) portal “Sede Electrónica” (e-Tax 2.0). Payment of any resulting liquid tax due simultaneously via PAIS (Plataforma de Servicios de Pago) or the web using the assigned 17-digit tax account reference.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. A timely corporates must also file an “Improvement Declaration” (Formulario 2A or 2B) only when updating net capital adjustments; no quarterly CIT installments for entities below the high-revenue threshold. For entities with annual taxable income above B/. 50 million, quarterly prepayment declarations are required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due on April 30 of the fiscal year following the calendar tax year. For non-calendar fiscal years, the due date is the last day of the fourth month after the fiscal year-end, unless a different date has been authorised by the DGI. Monthly advance withholding returns (for employees, vendors, rental payers, and dividend distributions) are required if applicable under Article 678 or under the specific regime of the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enters legal entity name, RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), DGI tax file number, and registered office residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an S.A. entirely owned by non-residents, provide the Panamanian registered agent number, in-country statutory address, and the constitutional mailing address. Never leave RUC blank; the company must first obtain RUC through DGI registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 – Renta Bruta de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue derived from Panamanian-source activities: sale of goods physically delivered or used in Panama, services performed in Panama, income from capital located in Panama, and operational income from domestic cloud contracts where server or payment infrastructure is accessed from Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an offshore cloud CRM entity without a Panamanian establishment, enter only revenue from contracts where the customer is resident in Panama and/or the cloud service is consumed in Panama. Non-resident cloud providers acting solely outside Panama exclude all foreign subscription receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 – Rentas Exentas y No Gravables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Lists exempt income: foreign-source income, interest from local banks for non-resident lenders without PE, capital gains on foreign shares, and dividends received from Panama corporations already subject to dividend tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident software outsourcing or intra-group service fees arising wholly outside Panama but remitted through Panama and not connected with a PE must be stated here with suffix code 110 to evidence the territorial exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs, operating expenses, depreciation, amortisation, and any deductions directly attributable to earning Panamanian-source income. Deductions must be documented, incurred for business purposes, and supported by accounting records and third-party invoices where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident without a Panamanian permanent establishment generally may not deduct head-office overheads or intercompany management fees from Panamanian-source royalties. For local software subcontractors or cloud hosting costs, the entity must obtain invoices from DGI-endorsed suppliers or a certified PA-recognised CSP receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after allowable deductions and applicable loss carry forwards. Panama allows no current-year loss deduction from foreign income; losses from Panamanian activities may be carried forward up to five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute this as solely Panama-source revenue less Panama-source allocable costs. Charges for senior management at the non-resident parent must be reallocated if the arm’s-length test is not met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 – Impuesto Determinado, Créditos y Retenciones
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax (25%) reduced by tax credits and withholding taxes previously borne such as 10% remittance tax, 5% interest withholding, or prepaid taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not permitted for non-resident holders without a PE. For Panama-source royalties taxed at 25% by remittance, the beneficiary may claim a reduced liquidation if a treaty applies, but cannot claim local foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 – Pago Neto o Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final payment due to the DGI or the carryable credit balance. Payment must be made by the same April 30 deadline, and no extension is granted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident taxpayer unable to file electronically due to invoicing or geographic constraints may request an agent mandate by filing a notarised power of attorney in the DGI web office. The agent should trigger the final payment in B/. on the same day.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly surcharge equal to 2% of the tax due, capped at 25% of that tax, plus late payment interest at the statutory bank rate (12% per annum under DGI practice; higher if the DGI determines a deliberate default). Failure to file a nil return: fixed penalty of B/. 150 to B/. 500 after notice. Failure to remit third-party withholdings (e.g., 25% remittance on foreign royalties): a 50% surcharge on the unremitted withholding plus criminal referral. Non-compliance with electronic filing can cause blockage of RUC and denial of licences.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% was the general statutory rate for dividends paid out of profits subject to corporate income tax; however, for distributions from profits that have already borne the 25% corporate tax (i.e., “fully taxed profits”), the dividend withholding acts as a final tax at the shareholder level, effectively the DGI receives a split: 10% directly on the dividend paid. Dividends paid out of tax-exempt foreign-source income of a Panama holding company are subject to a 0% rate if the company is not otherwise in a profit-distribution limitation; but distributions from a company benefiting from Panama Pacifico full exemption are subject to a 5% distribution tax at the time of remittance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama’s limited double-tax treaty network (e.g., agreements with Mexico, Netherlands, UK, France, Spain, UAE, among others) may reduce the dividend WHT to 5% if the beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the paid-in capital. The administrative protocol requires: (i) the foreign shareholder obtains a valid Colombian, Spanish, British, or other treaty-residency certificate (TRC) from its tax authority, stamped and certified within the previous 12 months; (ii) the Panama company provides a completed DGI form “Certificado de Residencia Fiscal / Anexo Tratado” plus a sworn declaration that the shareholder is the ultimate beneficial owner and is not subject to preferential regime in its home state; (iii) the DGI inspects both documents through the “Régimen Especial de Tributación Internacional” module in the Sede Electrónica before the reduced withholding can be applied; if the 10% has already been withheld, the foreign shareholder may apply for refund using the “Solicitud de Devolución de Retenciones” within 24 months after the end of the fiscal year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: under domestic law, Panamanian-source royalty payments to a non-resident (for use of IP, patents, software copyrights, or know-how commercially used in Panama) are subject to a 25% final withholding tax. Most DTAs reduce the rate to 10% where qualifying beneficial ownership is established and the IP is genuinely exploited abroad. Interest: interest paid to a non-resident lender is generally treated as foreign-source income and therefore subject to 0% withholding if the loan is made by an offshore bank or lender not engaged in business in Panama and no Panamanian permanent establishment is secured. Treaty relief for interest is not typically needed because the domestic rate is 0%; nevertheless, DTAs expressly protect the 0% treatment for interest paid to an enterprise of the treaty state.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 1,000,000 (one million Panamanian Balboas, equal to USD) aggregate related-party transactions during the taxable year triggers mandatory transfer-pricing documentation. Transactions between a local S.A. and a foreign parent or sister company (e.g., intra-group software licensing, cloud hosting fees, management charges, and the said CRM vertical’s intercompany service contracts) are covered. Additionally, the taxpayer must file an electronic informative return “Declaración Informativa de Transacciones con Partes Relacionadas” when annual related-party transactions exceed B/. 300,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP), commonly used for the cloud CRM licensing and intra-group shared service fees when third-party comparables are plentiful.
Resale Price Method, a second-tier approach for distribution platforms or resale of Gerencia de Relaciones con Clientes products.
Cost Plus Method, recommended for providing low-value-adding software development, IT support, and back-office services to the regional group.
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM), as the fallback profit-level indicator where no reliable gross-margin data can be identified, using the return on sales or capital employed.
Profit Split Method, appropriate for integrated cross-border software research and development and cloud-delivery platforms with unique intangible contributions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama tax authorities and business courts apply a “economic substance” doctrine to prevent perceived artificial structures. While no general statutory economic substance requirement yet applies to every S.A., the Tax Code (as reformed by Law 57 of 2018) requires that: (i) any deduction for intra-group payments must have a genuine business need and actual economic activity; (ii) “mannequin” or so-called shell corporations are subject to recharacterisation and the DGI may ignore legal personality where the company exists solely to avoid Panama-source taxes; (iii) the Tax Administration can apply the “place of effective management” test for classifying a Panama company as ultra-territorial when Board meetings and operational decisions are taken abroad. Financial criminal courts in Panama additionally consider the substance criteria under FATF-inspired AML/CFT measures, requiring a physical office, real employees, accounting records, and compliance with AML beneficial ownership reporting. Regular use under an offshore cloud structure without any local employees, local revenue operations, or proper governance will normally trigger compulsory liquidation under the “ley de licencia anual” or serve as evidence of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panamanian-source revenue from remote cloud contracts, false classification of software licensing as foreign-source income to escape the 25% corporate tax, overstatement of intercompany royalties to an Irish or Delaware affiliate, or failure to file Form 2 without a credible business premise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Panama Tax Code (Articles 1147, 1148, and 1181), the tax authority may impose up to 100% of the evaded tax differential, plus compound interest from the original due date. Additional fine for not filing the annual declaration: between 2% and 25% of the tax due. The evasion amount may be escalated for using fictitious invoices or shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing is permitted under Panama civil procedure when a director signs an incomplete or false tax return in bad faith or knowingly participates in hiding Panamanian-source income; such directors may be personally liable for restitution of the unpaid corporate tax, plus interest, and may face criminal imprisonment from 2 to 5 years and a lifetime prohibition from serving as a director in Panama if convicted of tax fraud involving amounts exceeding B/. 300,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Panama S.A. acting as a vertical CRM legal vehicle for a foreign cloud provider without employees, bank accounts in Panama, or any actual CRM service activity in the country, while claiming the benefit of the territorial regime for the entire revenue stream and potentially using Panamanian POA to funnel treaty flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI can disallow the entire claimed exemption, recharacterise 100% of the profits as Panamanian-source, and levy the 25% corporate rate plus 10% dividend withholding on unpaid distributions. The company may be struck off the Registro Público after two consecutive annual licence fees are unpaid; the Financial Intelligence Unit may issue a “destructive measure” freezing assets, and the tax authority may seek a judicial order for judicial dissolution of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an alleged shell may be held in civil restitution for intra-group assets approaching the company’s lost income, be barred from leaving Panama pending the criminal process, and face charges under Law 41 of 2000 and the Panama Criminal Code, Article 290, for false corporate declarations, with penalties of up to 6 years’ imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acting through the Panama S.A. as a cloud CRM subscription processor for third parties, allowing undisclosed beneficial owners, using nominee shareholders or bearer-certificate style documents, or processing subscription payments for a prohibited or politically exposed person while failing to file the Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Beneficiario) with the DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama’s Decree Law 12 of 2015, further reformed in 2018 and 2020, provides fines of up to B/. 5 million for a legal entity, suspension of the licence, and indefinite disqualification for officers. Failure to report beneficial ownership to the UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) is an infraction punishable by B/. 100,000 per non-filed report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial ownership declarations or knowingly allow undisclosed ownership expose themselves to civil penalties up to three times the financial loss generated, travel bans of up to 90 days at the request of the Public Ministry, and imprisonment from 3 to 7 years under Article 254-C of the Panamanian Penal Code for money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into cross-border controlled transactions (software royalty licence, marketing rebates, intercompany cloud hosting, loans) with values differing from market rates, or failing to maintain acceptable TP documentation when the B/. 1 million threshold is crossed, and not filing the informative return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI can adjust taxable income, deny deductions for excess royalty transfers, and impose a 10% penalty on the TP adjustment plus interest at the statutory bank rate. Should the adjustment exceed B/. 1 million, the DGI may treat the case as a serious infraction and apply a 25% surcharge. Failure to provide documentation within 45 business days of the DGI’s request triggers an automatic adverse inference and a separate fixed fine of B/. 10,000 to B/. 300,000, depending on the company’s size.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the TP policy was orchestrated by the parent company’s directors and supported by artificially low documentation, Panamanian courts may hold local directors jointly and severally liable for the tax adjustment, may issue an embargo of their personal property abroad, and, where intentional evasion is proven, can order their extradition to face criminal tax evasion charges carrying a 3 to 5-year prison sentence.
